title: Belgium Minimum Wage 2026: Tax, Mortgage Rates, Pension Age and Energy Prices Compared
content:
Updated 25 October 2026

Quick answer: In Belgium in 2026, the minimum wage is €2,234/month (about $2,501 a month full time); an average earner keeps 60% of their pay after income tax and social security; mortgage rates are about 3.7%; household electricity costs €0.357 per kWh; petrol is €1.99/L, up 32.2% since February. The table below puts 9 everyday money measures for Belgium side by side and ranks each one against the other countries in our data, using official figures from national statistics offices, central banks, the OECD and Eurostat.

Most comparisons of Belgium look at one number at a time. This page gathers the figures that matter for working, buying a home, paying bills and retiring in Belgium, so you can see them together and see how Belgium compares. Each section links to our full guide for that topic, which covers every country and lists the original sources, and each dataset can be downloaded free.

Minimum Wage in Belgium (2026)

The legal minimum wage in Belgium is €2,234/month. For a month of full-time work that is about $2,501 at current exchange rates, 7th highest of 38 countries in our comparison.

Full table for every country, with sources: Minimum Wage by Country 2026: Hourly and Monthly Rates in US Dollars. Download the data (CSV).

Income Tax and Take-Home Pay in Belgium

A single worker on the average wage in Belgium (about $88,000 at purchasing-power parity) pays 39.5% of gross pay in income tax and employee social security, so they keep 60%. That is the highest of 38 countries we compare, against an OECD average of 25.1%.

Income tax and employee social security take 39.5% of pay at the average wage, 31.5% at two-thirds of it and 47.4% at 1.67 times it. Including employer contributions, the total tax wedge is 52.5% of labour costs.

Full table for every country, with sources: Income Tax by Country 2026: How Much of Your Salary You Keep in 38 Countries. Download the data (CSV).

Mortgage Rates in Belgium (2026)

The typical mortgage rate in Belgium is 3.7% (new home loans, August 2026), 14th highest of 31 countries; the euro area average is 3.6%.

Up 0.23 points since February 2026 (3.47%). Monthly payment per €100,000 over 25 years: €511.

Full table for every country, with sources: Mortgage Rates by Country 2026: Where Buying a Home Costs the Most. Download the data (CSV).

Electricity Prices in Belgium

Households in Belgium pay about €0.357 per kWh of electricity (about $0.40), 3rd most expensive of 33 countries; the EU average is €0.283. Change: +2.2% vs late 2025.

Household gas: €0.085 per kWh. Typical household using 2,500–5,000 kWh a year, all taxes included, January–June 2026.

Full table for every country, with sources: Electricity Prices by Country 2026: What Households Pay per kWh, and What the Iran War Means for Bills. Download the data (CSV).

Petrol Prices in Belgium Since the Iran War

Petrol in Belgium costs €1.99/L (week of 19 October 2026), up 32.2% from €1.50/L in the week before the Iran war began. It peaked at €2.03/L (28 Sep). At about $2.23 a litre it is 10th most expensive of 29 countries, and the rise is 10th largest of 29 countries.

Full table for every country, with sources: Petrol Prices Since the Iran War: How Much They Have Risen in 35 Countries. Download the data (CSV).

Retirement Age in Belgium

The state pension age in Belgium is 66 for people reaching it in 2026; the earliest you can claim is Earlier with long careers. Future change: 67 in 2030.

Full table for every country, with sources: Retirement Age by Country 2026: State Pension Ages in 39 Countries. Download the data (CSV).

How Much the State Pension Pays in Belgium

A full-career average earner in Belgium can expect a mandatory pension worth about 61.1% of their previous net pay, 23rd least generous of 50 countries (OECD average 63.2%). Low earner (half the average wage): 81%. High earner (twice the average): 42%. Including common voluntary private pensions, an average earner would get 74%.

Full table for every country, with sources: State Pension Amounts by Country 2026: How Much Retirees Actually Get. Download the data (CSV).

How Much of Your Money Is Protected in Belgium

Bank deposits in Belgium are protected up to €100,000 per depositor, per bank (about $111,900), the limit set by EU law for every member state. Harmonised by EU law; local-currency equivalent outside the euro. Money in payment apps and e-money wallets is usually not covered.

Full table for every country, with sources: Deposit Insurance Limits by Country 2026: How Much of Your Money Is Protected. Download the data (CSV).

Inheritance Tax in Belgium

Belgium has inheritance tax (regional). Children can receive Low; varies by region tax-free, and the top rate for children is 27%, 9th highest of 28 countries. Flanders 3% to 27% for children; Brussels and Wallonia have higher top rates.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the minimum wage in Belgium in 2026?

The minimum wage in Belgium is €2,234/month, about $2,501 a month for full-time work. That is 7th highest of 38 countries.

How much tax do you pay in Belgium?

On the average wage, income tax plus employee social security in Belgium take 39.5% of gross pay, so a single worker keeps 60% (OECD average: 25.1%).

What are mortgage rates in Belgium right now?

Mortgage rates in Belgium are about 3.7% (new home loans, August 2026). Up 0.23 points since February 2026 (3.47%). Monthly payment per €100,000 over 25 years: €511.

How much does electricity cost in Belgium?

Household electricity in Belgium costs about €0.357 per kWh (about $0.40), 3rd most expensive of 33 countries.

How much has petrol gone up in Belgium?

Petrol in Belgium has risen 32.2% since February 2026, from €1.50/L to €1.99/L.

What is the retirement age in Belgium?

The state pension age in Belgium is 66 in 2026, with the earliest claim at Earlier with long careers. Legislated change: 67 in 2030.

How much is the state pension in Belgium?

In Belgium, mandatory pensions replace about 61.1% of an average earner's net pay after a full career, against an OECD average of 63.2%.

How much money is insured in a bank in Belgium?

Deposits in Belgium are insured up to €100,000 per person, per bank.

Is there inheritance tax in Belgium?

Yes. Children can inherit Low; varies by region tax-free in Belgium; above that the top rate for children is 27%.
